body.x: KDNA Co., Ltd. (CEO Dong-hwan Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

KDNA is realizing human care by integrating and developing expertise from various fields. They are conducting R&D of medical and beauty care-related devices thought their know-how of new material integration technology and hardware manufacturing. They aim to provide robust ‘humanwear’ services centered on consumer demands through the integration of new materials and IoT.

At the trade show, they mainly introduced a soft IR LED patch applying ‘stretchable technology’. As strengths of this patch, KDNA chose skin-adhesiveness, low power consumption, high efficiency, high skin penetration rate of the light, its integrated cosmetic band type, and a skin improvement effect that is 3 times faster. In addition, it is also characterized by being safe even when attached for a long time, due to its application of medical hydrocolloids, and allowing users to carry out normal activities even when applied on curved parts of the body. The module can be reused, and only the cosmetic band needs to be exchanged when reusing.

An official of KDNA said that, “Existing solid LED masks have poor efficiency due to the diffuse reflection from the skin due to the distance between the light source and the skin. In contrast, the near-infrared LED patch reduces factors that reduce light penetration from diffuse reflection from the skin, and had good efficiency, even with low power consumption,” and explained that, “In addition, existing LED patches need to solder LED to FPCB and is stiff due to the characteristics of FPCB (PI), making it hard to adhere closely to the curved surface of the face. However, KDNA developed a source technology that solders LED onto stretchable PCB to solve these issues, and created a product with a new concept.”

They went on to say, “Though stretchable technology is currently being developed competitively in industries and academia around the world, but is still in the early stages. KDNA is proud to be leading the commercialization of products applied with stretchable technology with our own technology and process, from material to module,” and said that, “Though our participation of the upcoming CES, we plan to raise awareness of our company and technology, discover B2B partners and attract overseas investment.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
